what: Against the engine as of 12:05 today, cpp ch26 fails the checker at 390. Its three tilted sketch panels (.tilt-l/.tilt-r) poke 4-6px past the page column, so the gutter is lost on that side. The same classes are used in ch27 and ch28 (and book-wide), so this is an engine issue, not a chapter one.

Cause: assets/ext/cpp-ch26.js idabouncer `fitSize(label, 52, 12, 7)`, a 12-unit maximum on a 200-unit viewBox drawn at 128-170px wide. what: `.vs td code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` breaks C++ names in the middle, even at desktop width.
evidence: P28 at 1280: 'std::ranges::random_a|ccess_range' breaks between 'a' and 'ccess'. Rule: ext/cpp-ch26.css `.vs td code, .vs th code { font-weight: 800; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`
fix: `.vs td code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → `overflow-wrap: break-word`, plus `<wbr>` after each `::` in the long names (why: break-word only breaks when nothing else fits. A break at `::` keeps the name readable as a qualified name)

what: The 'which tool for which trouble' table is cut off at the right edge on phones, with nothing to say it scrolls. The visible names break in the middle ('std::optiona|l', 'std::expecte|d', 'std::from_ch|ars').

fix: Add `@media (max-width:640px){ .vs.wide td code { overflow-wrap: normal; white-space: nowrap } }` and wrap the table as `<div class="vswrap picscroll">` (or add the engine's swipe hint) (why: whole identifiers, and a visible cue that the table scrolls sideways)

what: The ticket rail numbers its tickets from 0, while the narration ('Step N of 8'), the aria-live line and the text-version table count from 1. So at 'Step 5 of 8' the ticket marked NOW is ticket 4, and in the transcript the same ticket is row 5.
evidence: Stepped P13 four times: narration 'Step 5 of 8', `.rail-step.now .tno` = '4', transcript first row = '1'. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-26-29/rail-390.png. Cause: assets/ext/cpp-ch29.js `'' + k + ''` (k is the step index, and step 0 is the start), while render() uses `st.step + 1` and the transcript uses `k + 1`.
fix: `'<span class="tno">' + k` → `'<span class="tno">' + (k + 1)`, so the ticket number equals the step number everywhere (why: one number per moment, the same in the picture, the narration and the text version)

panel: ch26 P18, ch27 P17, ch28 P17, ch29 P35 (.pair2)
what: All four chapters' CSS has `.pair2 .term { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }`. That bypasses the engine's terminal wrapping, so side-by-side terminals wrap at any character with no hanging indent. Continuation lines start at column 0 and look like new commands.
evidence: ch28 P17 at 390: '-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -g -c' and 'main.cpp price.cpp menu.cpp' start flush left under the prompt, while engine .term.wrap terminals elsewhere on the page indent their continuations. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-26-29/c28-p17-390.png. Rules: cpp-ch26.css:13, cpp-ch27.css:17, cpp-ch28.css:10, cpp-ch29.css:18. (The separate `.term.wrap` duplicates are already listed in engine-refresh-chapter-todo §1 and are not re-reported.)
fix: `.pair2 .term { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` → delete it, and write `class="term wrap"` on the pair2 terminals (why: the engine's hanging indent shows that a wrapped line continues the command above. `anywhere` also splits file names)

panel: ch27 P21, P26, P30 (cards4/settings); ch29 P2, P45 (cards4/bookwall), P13/P16 (.ticket)
what: Hand-rolled cards copy the engine's `.duo-card` card with raw values instead of tokens. `.card4` (4px 4px 0 shadow, 14px radius), `.settings li`/`.anatomy li` (3px 3px 0, 10px), `.ticket` (2px 2px 0, 8px) and `.bookwall li` (12px radius) each have their own shadow and radius.
evidence: ext/cpp-ch27.css `.card4 { … border-radius: 14px; … box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink) }`, `.settings li { … border-radius: 10px; … box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 var(--ink) }`. ext/cpp-ch29.css `.card4` (same), `.ticket { … border-radius: 8px; … box-shadow: 2px 2px 0 var(--ink) }`, `.bookwall li { border-radius: 12px }`. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 maps Card → `.duo-card` with `--radius-lg` and `--shadow-hard`.
fix: `.card4 { border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink) }` → `<div class="duo-card">` in a `.duo` grid, or at least `border-radius: var(--radius-lg); box-shadow: var(--shadow-hard)` (and `--radius-md`/`--shadow-hard` for .settings li, .ticket, .bookwall li) (why: one card system book-wide, and later token changes reach these pages)

panel: ch26 P8/P11 (.anatomy), ch28 P7/P13/P20/P22 (.anatomy), ch28 P32 (.mangled)
what: `.anatomy li` and `.mangled li` are hand-rolled key cards with raw shadow and radius values (3px 3px 0, 10px/8px), and ch28's `.mangled li:nth-child(even)` alternates dashed borders as decoration. They duplicate the engine's anatomy styling and break the rule that a dashed border means something (an optional or once-only item).
evidence: ext/cpp-ch26.css and ext/cpp-ch28.css `.anatomy li { … border-radius: 10px; … box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 var(--ink); }`. cpp-ch28.css `.mangled li:nth-child(even) { background: var(--cream); border-style: dashed; }`. The same pages use dashed for '.opt' / 'ONE item only' cards.
fix: `box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 var(--ink); border-radius: 10px` → `box-shadow: var(--shadow-hard); border-radius: var(--radius-md)`. For `.mangled li:nth-child(even) { border-style: dashed }` → keep the solid border and alternate only the fill (why: dashed is the book's signal for 'optional / lasts once'. Decorative dashing dilutes it)
